chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man from the Children of Israel worshipped Allah for forty years. Then he offered an offering, but it was not accepted from him. So he said to himself, "It has not come to you except from yourself, and there is no sin except for you." He said: "So Allah, Blessed and High, revealed unto him: Your condemning yourself is superior to your worship for forty years."'
ai.seo_question: Why was the man's worship rejected despite forty years of devotion?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (as) illustrates the profound Shia emphasis on *muhasaba* (self-accounting) and humility, revealing that sincere recognition of one's spiritual deficiency outweighs prolonged but potentially prideful ritualism. This narrative underscores the principle that the quality of one's internal state and self-awareness is superior to the mere quantity of external worship, a key concept in Shia asceticism (*zuhd*).
